entries.name: CBOT Maize
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of CBOT Maize as of June 24 decreased by 10.3% MOM and declined by 1.7% YOY to $161.93/MT. According to market participants, recent rainfall in June across the western US Corn Belt has boosted soil moisture levels and improved crop conditions. entries.name: CBOT Wheat
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of CBOT Wheat as of June 24 decreased by 6.9% MOM and rose by 8.8% YOY to $218.23/MT. Overall, the month-on-month decline reflected the market's transition from old-crop to new-crop supplies, with approaching harvest availability adding seasonal pressure to prices. However, poor US crop conditions provided some underlying support during June. According to the latest USDA Crop Progress report, only 27% of winter wheat was rated good-to-excellent, compared with 52% at the same point last year. Meanwhile, harvest progress reached 25%, well ahead of last year's 9%. Market participants noted that the accelerated harvest pace could indicate weaker yield potential, particularly following prolonged drought stress.

entries.name: EU Rapeseed
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of EU Rapeseed as of June 24 decreased by 2.5% MOM and rose by 3.4% YOY to €510.35/MT. Market players said sentiment into July remains broadly firm, but the tone is being driven more by unresolved supply risk than by any settled conviction over where the EU crop will finally land. Sources said the market still lacks clarity on whether the EU crop stabilizes near current official assumptions or continues to move lower toward the latest JRC MARS yield path, and that uncertainty is keeping buyers, crushers and short-covering participants active even at harvest. Several market players said the market still looks potentially tight overall, particularly because a lower EU crop could immediately reopen the import question at a time when external seed cover still looks less straightforward than the official balance suggests.

Ukrainian sunflower sowing reached only 86.8% of the forecast area as of June 2, with 4,341.9k ha planted against a target of 5,000.4k ha, while a deep farmer-crusher standoff left an estimated 3.5-3.7 million tonnes for June in farm storage moving at minimal pace toward processing, with sources saying crusher forward coverage of just 0.4-0.6 million tonnes and deeply negative crush margins have created conditions where material is not flowing through the supply chain in a manner consistent with seasonal norms. entries.name: Euronext Maize
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Euronext Maize as of June 24 decreased by 0.6% MOM and rose by 11.5% YOY to €219.10/MT. Extreme heat and dryness affected Western Europe in June, particularly France, with these conditions gradually spreading eastwards, although the impact remained less severe outside Western Europe. According to market participants, France entered a critical stage of crop development during the month, with early maize pollination taking place under exceptionally hot and dry conditions. Temperatures exceeded 40°C in some areas, increasing crop stress and making some yield losses increasingly unavoidable. Market participants told Expana that French maize acreage was already expected to decline this season, making final yield performance even more important for overall production.

entries.name: US Chicken
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of US Chicken as of June 24 decreased by 3.3% MOM and declined by 12.8% YOY to $2,608.70/MT. Monthly US broiler production continued to trend above year-ago levels, though month-over-month production retreated lower. Demand throughout June was somewhat limited, though pockets of active wing demand emerged lout of distributive and foodservice channels. Extreme heat across much of the country further dampened consumer engagement heading into the holiday weekend, with buyers largely considered to have wrapped up July 4, procurement ahead of schedule and distributors continuing to operate on a hand-to-mouth basis.

entries.paragraph: In May, the average price of Norwegian Haddock decreased by 19.3% MOM and rose by 10.4% YOY to NOK 25,781.55/MT. The white fish market in Europe has been under supply pressure as the availability of Atlantic cod and pollock has been reported to be lower. This has sustained YOY price increases for Atlantic haddock, despite the total allowed catch in the Barents Sea increasing 18% YOY in 2026. Haddock landings continue to show recovery, with landings higher YOY in the first three months of the year. According to the Norwegian Directorate of Fisheries, accumulated landings through May showed a 2.9% YTD increase to 42,562 MT.

entries.name: Chilean Salmon
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Chilean Salmon as of June 24 decreased by 6.8% MOM and rose by 12.2% YOY to $13.67/kg. The Chilean salmon market in the USA has exhibited a downward price trend, which market participants attribute to an unsettled market tone and weak to mixed demand signals. However, YOY prices remain higher than in 2025 and above the three-year average. This may be linked to a stronger international outlook for Chilean salmon, particularly in key markets such as Brazil and Asia. According to the Undersecretariat for Fisheries and Aquaculture (SUBPESCA), accumulated harvest through April 2026 totaled 257,467 MT, a 16.5% YTD increase compared to the same period in 2025.

entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of Shrimp Asian Whiteleg as of June 24 decreased by 5.8% MOM and declined by 6.0% YOY to $8.90/kg. CFR prices for ASian peeled vannamei into Europe have been drifting down since January, driven by softer demand, with the decline accelerating in May as spring-season supply added volume to the market. Farm-gate prices have eased slightly, but rising input costs—energy, transport and feed—have compressed producer margins. As a result, export prices held broadly steady in June, with sellers adopting a wait-and-see posture for positive signs of replacement demand ahead of the summer season.

entries.name: US Apple
entries.paragraph: The average weekly price of US Apple as of June 24 decreased by 0.9% MOM and rose by 21.2% YOY to $0.74/Lb. The US apple market remains steady but tighter than last year in some varieties. Washington still has solid supplies, especially Honeycrisp, while Red Delicious and Gala are more limited, and Eastern inventories are also tightening with little uncommitted fruit available. Demand is healthy, led by premium varieties and strong processing interest. The Washington State Tree Fruit Association said it will end early-season crop estimates, citing poor accuracy and concern that inflated forecasts have hurt pricing. Meanwhile, proposed H-2A reforms could also improve labor availability for growers.

Prices have spiked with the onset of the new season, as is typical due to a usual dip in supply. entries.paragraph: The average weekly spot price of ICE London Cocoa futures as of June 24 increased by 15.5% MOM and decreased by 42.5% YOY to £3,432.20/MT, while the average weekly spot price of ICE New York Cocoa futures as of June 24 increased by 13.2% MOM and decreased by 51.4% YOY to $4,451.60/MT. Cocoa prices rallied sharply in June as the poor pod counts in West Africa were bolstered by ongoing fears that the developing El Niño could potentially be a very strong event in the later part of the year. There was also uncertainty over production volumes from Ivory Coast and Ghana as supply estimates continue to be revised. In turn, there was then renewed buying as sentiment turned more bullish.

Larger sizes including WW240 and WW180 continued drawing support from steady demand and limited availability, with momentum likely also spilling into WW320.

entries.name: Turkish dried apricot
entries.paragraph: Turkish dried apricot prices were unchanged MOM in June at $9,250/MT, down 9.8% YOY. Prospects for the new season crop in Turkey appear promising, with early offers suggesting further softness ahead in the spot market.

entries.paragraph: In June, the average price of US Testliner increased by 6.4% MOM and rose by 6.4% YOY to $0.42/Lb. Softening feedstock cost gives recycled linerboard producers a modest margin tailwind even as finished product prices rise, though OCC remains roughly 4-5% above year-ago levels. Kruger restarted its roughly 363,000 MT/year Machine No. 10 at the Trois-Rivières mill in Quebec around June 20 after a three-week strike, returning high-performance recycled linerboard capacity to the market.

entries.name: US Cartonboard FBB
entries.paragraph: In June, the average price of US Cartonboard FBB was unchanged MOM and rose by 3.0% YOY to $0.69/Lb. Elevated transatlantic freight costs tied to the broader Middle East-driven logistics disruption continue to impact imported FBB price dynamics relative to competing grades.

entries.name: LME Aluminium
entries.paragraph: In June, the average 3m futures price of LME Aluminium decreased by 4.4% MOM and rose by 36.6% YOY to $3,438.89/MT. The fall in aluminium prices was the steepest among base metals, driven by the resumption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried approximately 8% of global exports before the strait's closure. Based on price dynamics late in the month, many sources expect price declines to continue as shipping operations fully recover.

entries.name: EU LDPE
entries.paragraph: In June, the average price of EU LDPE decreased by 3.3% MOM and rose by 53.9% YOY to €2,921.75/MT. Easing geopolitical tensions resulted in declining ethylene prices, which in turn lowered product prices. According to market sources, demand was poor with the approaching summer holidays, while imports from Asian origins arriving into the EU increased throughout June.

entries.name: US LDPE
entries.paragraph: In June, the average price of US LDPE decreased by 3.7% MOM and rose by 8.9% YOY to USc 104/Lb. The continued decline in ethylene prices resulted in decreasing LDPE prices in the US, as manufacturers were no longer able to justify price increases as was the case during the most challenging periods of the Middle East conflict.

entries.name: US PET
entries.paragraph: In June, the average price of US PET decreased by 5.0% MOM and rose by 13.1% YOY to USc 71.25/Lb. Falling production costs lowered product prices, although product prices remain elevated compared to pre-war levels. Demand was strong, according to market participants, especially from drinks manufacturers.

entries.name: US PP
entries.paragraph: In June, the average price of US PP decreased by 3.3% MOM and declined by 0.3% YOY to USc 73.75/Lb. PP prices continued to move downwards throughout the month, attributable to lower feedstock costs and more balanced supply and demand environment. Export demand also cooled down compared to the dynamic in previous months.
